Retrieve your first context

Use the configured scenario “Permission Wall” with its Analyst document role.

Retrieve evidence returns selected document fragments. Generate answer sends that context to the configured model. The result records the executed query and effective role. Editing the input does not change that result until you run it again.

Step 4 of 6

Exit
Compare permission and policy decisions

Run the current question through Top-k, Permissions Only and Full Policy. The same question and role can produce different context because each policy applies different selection rules.

Choose Run policy comparison below, then inspect the three columns. Look for sources included by Top-k that Full Policy blocks for your role. Some questions and roles have no permission difference.

Step 5 of 6

Exit
Follow a Full Policy decision

Open Decision Trace to see why each fragment was included, blocked or excluded. In Compare, this opens Full Policy: the policy that checks permissions, freshness and the context budget.

A superseded source can lose priority and still be included if it fits. A document can be partially included when only some of its fragments fit. Read the reason beside each outcome.

From retrieved context to an answer

Generate answer sends selected context to a configured model and returns an answer. Any extra prompt trimming is disclosed. Citation identifiers are checked against sent context; this does not prove every claim.

Generate answer: available; requires an explicit click and may incur provider cost.
Upload: requires an administrator and enabled ingestion.
Audit: available for the current workspace and authorized scope.
Evaluations: inspect benchmark completion, failures and denominators.

Reopen or restart this guide from Guide at any time.
